title: Catalog entity registration
description: One YAML file onboards ONE entity of ANY kind (requirement §10). Supersedes service.schema.json, which could only describe a service: `kind`, `platform`, `env`, `region`, `criticality`, `monitoring_profile`, `slo.profile`, `oncall` and typed `dependencies` are the fields §10 asks for and the service schema rejected. Every field the service schema accepted is still accepted here, under the same name except `tier` → `criticality` (the §10 name; the resolver maps it straight back onto the `tier` tag, so no telemetry contract changes).

kind.description: What this thing IS. Governs which Datadog entity kind is emitted — see platform/policy/entity_kinds.yaml, which also records why `frontend_app` and `repository` do not map 1:1 onto a Datadog kind.

name.description: Catalog identity. For a service-shaped entity this MUST equal the `service` tag on its telemetry, or every archetype that groups by {service} reports it as a different thing.

team.description: Owning team handle; must exist in platform/policy/teams.yaml. This is the ROUTING owner.

owner.description: Accountable owner — a person or distribution list. Optional: defaults to the owning team's email. Kept separate from `team` because the team is who gets paged and the owner is who answers for the thing existing.

oncall.description: Who carries the pager for this entity when that is NOT simply the owning team (a shared datastore owned by data-engineering but carried by the DBA rotation, for example).

criticality.description: The §10 name for what the tag standard calls `tier`. Same vocabulary, same consequences: profile, band, paging, SLO scope, support model.

platform.description: The technology this runs ON — azure_sql, azure_service_bus, aks, vmware, snowflake, dotnet. Emitted as the entity's `spec.type` and as a `platform:` tag; it is the §9 `platform` inheritance layer made explicit.

domain.description: Technology domain (platform/policy/domains.yaml). Optional: derived from `service_archetype` when one is declared, which is why a queue or a system — neither of which has an archetype — usually sets it explicitly.

service_archetype.description: Selects the monitor packs (platform/policy/service_archetypes.yaml). Required for the kinds whose monitoring comes from packs; meaningless for a system.

envs.description: Every environment this entity exists in.

env.description: The environment the CATALOG ENTRY represents. Datadog holds one catalog entity per name, not one per environment, so the catalog describes production unless told otherwise. Must be one of `envs`.

region.description: Primary region — an Azure region name, or `global`.

lifecycle.description: Datadog `spec.lifecycle`. `deprecated` is how an entity stops being scored without being deleted.

monitoring_profile.description: OVERRIDE only. Normally derived from criticality via platform/policy/tiers.yaml; an entity that needs a different profile in steady state needs an approved exception (platform/policy/exceptions.yaml), not this field.

profile.description: Which SLO regime applies. Vocabulary is tiers.yaml's `slo.scope`; defaults to the tier's own scope. Per-objective overrides are Phase 4.

dependencies.description: What this entity needs to work. Each item is either a bare entity name (`orders-sql`) or an explicit `kind:name` reference (`datastore:orders-sql`); the resolver turns bare names into references by looking the name up in platform/entities/ and falling back to `service:` — deterministically, never by guessing from the string.

components.description: For `kind: system` only — the entities the system is made of. Membership is declared HERE and nowhere else, so `componentOf` on each member is derived, not maintained twice.

owns.description: For `kind: repository` only — the entities whose code lives here. A repository emits no Datadog entity of its own (entity_kinds.yaml records why); it contributes a `repo` link to each entity it owns.

idempotent.description: Whether re-running/retrying this entity's work is safe — read by the automation safety contract (platform/policy/workflows.yaml).

allOf.$comment: Pack-driven kinds must say which packs apply. A system has no telemetry of its own and a queue/api is monitored by the messaging and synthetic packs through its platform, not through an archetype.
A system is defined by what it contains; an empty one is a label, not an entity.
Only service-shaped kinds carry dependsOn in the v3 spec (EntityV3ServiceSpec). Accepting `dependencies` on a datastore or queue would mean writing YAML the API silently discards.
`components`, `owns` and `repository_url` belong to exactly one kind each.
